All eight cells already carry a canonical verdict (seven from run 39557190033, meriyah from its recovery run 39585210102) and each already received one extra attempt in 39620264048. This manifest declares one further attempt per cell under the variance-check class, with the frozen per-cell official budget, the same grader and the same generation parallelism. It does not replace any verdict and no cell receives a second extra attempt in this manifest.

constraints: One predeclared headless attempt per cell; no cell receives a second extra attempt in this manifest.
Every verdict of run 39557190033, of recovery run 39585210102 and of the reproduction run 39620264048 is preserved and never replaced, repaired or reinterpreted by this batch.
This batch produces no pass@1 and its counts are never merged into any rate; the official figure for run 39557190033 stays its declared repaired pass rate over its own predeclared task set.

Same provider, same effort, same per-cell official budgets, same grader and same generation parallelism as the source run; the declared deltas are the candidate (three text-only tool-contract slices) and the meriyah image transport.
No budget, timeout or effort is extended to make any cell scoreable.

The disposition is recorded but is not the primary question: the three fixes change model-visible text only, so a disposition flip is possible but not predicted, and a flip is never attributed to a capability change.

knownRisks.providerTransport: The baseline run recorded seven transport stalls across five cells for 1181 seconds (largest-eigenval 550 s of a 900 s budget, chess-best-move 435 s). A recurrence costs a cell its verdict exactly as measured and is disclosed, never retried; it also makes the tool-call tally noisier because a stalled cell issues fewer calls.
knownRisks.textOnlyFixes: The three merged slices change description text only. A zero change in the waste count is therefore a possible outcome and must be reported as such rather than explained away, and the sample is one attempt per cell on one provider profile — it can show that a waste shape did or did not recur, never a rate.
knownRisks.meriyahSpecGap: meriyah's only remaining fail-to-pass case is the declared specification gap (how a for-of head is disambiguated when the binding itself is named `of`). No text fix in this candidate addresses it, so a pass there is not predicted.
knownRisks.budget: Each cell keeps the official budget the source run declared; none is extended.
knownRisks.finality: One attempt per cell. A cell that dies again keeps no new verdict and its source verdict still stands.

plannedChecks: After the report artifact is downloaded, read it with the same metric code used for 39620264048 (dedup tool calls by callId across terminal snapshots) so the comparison is apples to apples: per cell the tool-call count, hard rejections by code, ran-and-failed closures, shell operators passed as literal argv to a non-shell exec, args[0] repeating the command name, transport stall seconds, write calls and whether the verifier's deliverable path was ever named; then the eight dispositions and budgets against the predeclared baseline table above, the candidate receipt (one frozen candidate, its three tool-contract slices present in the built source), usage, and evidence sha256 checks. Expected observable effect, predeclared: the shell-operator and repeated-command shapes should stop appearing in the argument shapes (or recur — either result is recorded verbatim), and no cell's outcome may be attributed to a capability change. Then a short record beside the two existing ones; no .official.json is written for this batch.
